name: S-40503

card.summary: A preclinical nonsteroidal SARM tested in rat osteoporosis models; known mainly from doping-control research, with no human efficacy data.
card.note: Preclinical only; detectable in doping tests.

quick.overview:
S-40503 is an experimental nonsteroidal selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM). It was described in 2003 in rat models of osteoporosis, where it showed bone-building activity.

No human clinical trials are listed in the sources consulted. It is discussed mainly in anti-doping analytical literature.
quick.mechanism: It binds the androgen receptor with nanomolar affinity and preferentially over other nuclear receptors. In orchiectomized rats given it for 4 weeks, researchers evaluated its bone effects against dihydrotestosterone.
quick.risks: No human safety data are described. SARMs are prohibited by WADA, and doping-control laboratories have developed methods to detect S-40503 in human plasma.

lead: S-40503 is an experimental nonsteroidal selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM), a compound designed to switch on androgen receptors in muscle and bone while leaving tissues such as the prostate less affected. The pitch for this class in physique communities is muscle and bone gain without the full effects of testosterone, which is why S-40503 is listed among SARMs in forum discussion of lean mass and body composition. [1][4]

It was first described in 2003. In castrated rats given S-40503 for four weeks, femoral bone mineral density and muscle weight (levator ani) rose about as much as with dihydrotestosterone (DHT), while prostate weight did not rise above normal; DHT raised prostate weight about 1.5-fold. In ovariectomised rats treated for two months it increased cortical bone density and strength. [1] It bound the androgen receptor with nanomolar affinity, preferentially among nuclear receptors. [1]

Later literature on it comes mostly from doping control, where laboratories developed plasma tests for it as an emerging drug with misuse potential. [2][3] SARMs as a class were added to the WADA Prohibited List in 2008, and none has received full clinical approval. [3] No human trial of S-40503 was found.
infobox: Osteoporosis; described as suited to bone with low virilisation [1][4]

paras: S-40503 preferentially bound the androgen receptor over other nuclear receptors in the 2003 report, and its effects were compared with the natural steroid DHT. [1] Wikipedia describes SARMs generally as acting like agonists in muscle and bone but as partial agonists or antagonists in tissues such as the prostate; the mechanism of this selectivity is still debated. [5]

In orchiectomised rats treated for four weeks, bone mineral density of the femur and muscle weight of the levator ani increased as markedly as with DHT, without enlarging the prostate. Four-week treatment of normal rats did not enlarge the prostate. In ovariectomised rats treated for two months, it raised cortical bone density and biomechanical strength, whereas estrogen did not. [1]

Wikipedia reports that SARMs have been studied for muscle wasting, osteoporosis and other conditions. Several trials show increased lean mass, but improved strength or function is less clear, and neither the FDA nor the EMA had approved a SARM as of 2023. [5] In bodybuilding communities SARMs are used for their anabolic effects, with gains described as generally smaller than with moderate testosterone doses; elevated liver enzymes, lowered HDL cholesterol and hormonal suppression have been reported with some SARMs. [5]

A 2009 study developed plasma methods to identify S-40503 alongside GW501516, S-107 and JTV-519 as emerging drugs with misuse potential. [3] A 2018 review notes that SARMs were added to WADA's Prohibited List in 2008 and that numerous adverse analytical findings have since been reported for various SARMs, though none has full clinical approval. [2]

S-40503 appears in a T Nation discussion of Ostarine as an item in a list of SARMs, described as selective for bone with particularly low virilisation and intended for osteoporosis. [4] Wikipedia notes that SARMs are sold online as research chemicals and that a study found most products advertised as SARMs were mislabelled. [5]
No studies found. Published work is limited to rat studies of bone and muscle effects [1] and analytical doping-control methods. [2][3]

lore.intro: S-40503 is rarely discussed on its own; it appears mostly in lists of SARMs.

claims.claim: S-40503 is a bone-selective SARM with low virilisation
claims.believers: A T Nation list describes it as selective for bone tissue, particularly low virilising, intended for osteoporosis and possibly suited to women.[4]
claims.experts: The 2003 rat study reported bone and muscle gains without prostate enlargement; no human study has tested it.[1]

angle.text: People interested in physique discuss SARMs as muscle-building alternatives to anabolic steroids. For S-40503, the data are limited to rats, where it raised muscle weight and bone density, with the original authors highlighting bone and low virilising activity.
